gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the three shown cameras list the same kind of US LTE band set, yet their makers' carrier claims differ. eufy says the S330's included SIM runs on AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon. Reolink's Go PT Ultra spec table recommends only T-Mobile and AT&T prepaid data (plus FreedomPop and Mint), even though its marketing copy names Verizon. ANRAN tells G1 buyers who bring their own SIM to pick T-Mobile or AT&T.
standout_why: I compared four pages. Buffalo Alarm (cited) has battery, solar, data cost and price per model, but no bands and no carrier per model; it only says AT&T and Verizon have the broadest rural coverage. Reolink's 4G solar guide (cited) gives the Go PT Ultra's bands and says it uses 'AT&T, Verizon or T-Mobile, whichever signal is strongest', which repeats the marketing claim and leaves out the product spec table that drops Verizon. It covers no eufy or ANRAN models. SecurityCamHQ (rank 1) quantifies neither battery nor carriers for the Go PT Ultra, and mentions only T-Mobile, for the Go PT Plus. None of these pages puts the carrier support for the three products ChatGPT showed side by side, and none lists battery-life claims with their test conditions.
decides: Verizon is often the only usable signal on rural land, and that is the main use case here. If so, the eufy 4G LTE Cam S330 is the one candidate whose maker page states Verizon support without contradicting itself, and it is the only one with a solar panel built in (4.5 W). ChatGPT's 'best overall', the Reolink Go PT Ultra, has an unresolved Verizon contradiction on its own page, and ChatGPT's budget ANRAN G1 is limited to T-Mobile or AT&T when you use your own SIM. Where AT&T or T-Mobile coverage is strong, the pick doesn't change.
